newsitem.title: UK: MAM to launch new trust in retail push.
newsitem.headline: MAM to launch new trust in retail push.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management Plc said on Monday it would launch an investment trust aimed at the retail market to be managed by its institutional fund management team.

MAM Investment Trust's managing director Lough Callahan said the Mercury Retirement Trust would offer a clear alternative to additional voluntary contributions (AVC) on pensions, and represented a potential strong growth area for group.
"Mercury's core business will remain institutional business but the opportunity for growth is in the retail and international side," said Callahan.

MAM aims to raise between 50 and 75 million stg for the trust, which will offer two separately managed classes of share, growth and income. Investors will be able to switch between the two shares without penalty.
He expected a prospectus for the trust in June and a closing in July.
Callahan said many investors were reluctant to use AVCs because of the lock-up on their capital, and the trust would offer an alternative vehicle, although it did not have the same tax advantages.

MAM has recently moved to integrate its retail operations with its core institutional business. Analysts have said that MAM must tap the growing retail pension market, and grow its international business if it is to maintain its strong industry position.
At end-September, MAM had nearly 86 billion sterling under management. It reports annual results for the year to end-March on Thursday.
